text: My family and I had our teeth cleaned. The service was excellent. They even sent us off with a smile. However, the level of care was unimaginable in Japan. The cleaning was brutal and painful. Even in Japan, removing tartar near the gums can cause bleeding and pain, but nothing like that. The doctor also wiped our faces with a wet towel, which was unhygienic and unpleasant. I don't think this was the case in Japan even 40 years ago. My biggest regret is having my child treated first, not realizing that something like this would happen. I hesitate to leave a negative review, but I thought it would be better to comment when I think about the people who have had their teeth removed by that doctor. I can't help but wonder if there's a problem...

text:
I had a ceramic filling on a broken molar treated here. The Japanese language support was also good when making an appointment, so I felt at ease. Dr. Pongsak treated me, and he spoke fluent Japanese. His treatment plan was easy to understand, and it almost felt like I was being treated at a Japanese dentist. The appointment took about 30 minutes, and the treatment was completed in one day, which I was very grateful for. The treatment cost 2,100 baht, but I don't think it's too expensive. The only downside is that it's a little far from the BTS station. It's closer from Thonglor. It's nice to be able to shop at Fuji Supermarket on the way back, though.
As an aside, I was surprised to find that the man at the reception desk was fluent in Chinese (he was dealing with Chinese customers). He also seemed to speak English, so it seems like they can provide services in four languages.

restaurant_name: พรศักดิ์ทันตแพทย์ PORNSAK DENTAL CLINIC
text:
This dentist on Sukhumvit 49 is popular with many Japanese people. There are several dentists catering to Japanese people in Bangkok's Phrom Phong and Thonglor areas, but this is one of the more popular.

When you call, you'll be surprised to hear, "Hello, this is the dentist..." but you can make an appointment in Japanese. It's not that the staff are rude, they just don't speak Japanese that well. They were fully booked for about a week, so I made an appointment for the earliest available date and time.

The staff can also speak Japanese, so it's reassuring. I was worried the fees would be extremely high, but I was pleased that they weren't that expensive: 100 baht for the consultation, 1,500 baht for simple cavity treatment, and 1,500 baht for tartar removal.

restaurant_name: พรศักดิ์ทันตแพทย์ PORNSAK DENTAL CLINIC
text:
Visited on September 13, 2019.
Among the many dentists in Bangkok, this is a well-known dentist with an established reputation among Japanese people.
As a frequent visitor to many veterans who have lived in Bangkok for over 20 years, this dentist is a must-visit when it comes to reasonable treatment fees, quality of treatment, and the peace of mind of knowing they can communicate in Japanese.
There may be better dentists in Bangkok, but this is my personal choice.
Fluent Japanese is a challenge, but communication is sufficient with simple Japanese.
If you encounter a dentist who doesn't speak Japanese, a Japanese-speaking staff member will act as an interpreter.
However, since this is not an ultra-high-end dentist, you may be somewhat overwhelmed... But the peace of mind of having an interpreter, even if just for a brief moment, is great.
I had a filling reattached to a missing tooth for 900 baht (3,200 yen), a full self-pay fee not covered by insurance.
I also had tartar removed for the same 900 baht.
I'm happy that simple treatments can be completed in a day.

text:
Japanese OK

I use this dentist. Japanese OK. They require an appointment, but if you're in pain and just pop in, they'll help you. When you call, they'll initially speak Thai, but if they realize you're speaking Japanese or Thai spoken by a Japanese person, they'll switch to Japanese. The dentists also speak Japanese, and a nurse will accompany you as an interpreter.

In Thailand, a typical visit to the dentist is a one-time affair, but dental care is handled by specialized dentists, such as cavity treatment, anesthesia, and tooth extractions. Even if you pop in, if the dentist isn't there, you'll just get first-aid and have to go again.

It's more expensive than a local dentist, but cheaper than a major private hospital. Insurance is accepted.
